title: The missed approach
summary: Fog below minimums at Kennedy: fly the ILS to 200 ft, and when there is no runway, go around by the book.
briefing: Kennedy is in fog: a hundred-foot ceiling, a quarter of a mile. Our minimums are two hundred feet.
We fly the ILS down to minimums. If we can't see the runway there, we go around: TO GA, the T key, climb away, gear up, flaps twenty. Going around is never a failure. Landing when you shouldn't is.

tasks.done: Armed. Now we fly it down.

tasks.goal: Fly the ILS down to 300 ft.
tasks.say: Gear down when the glideslope's alive, landing flaps, and down the ILS. Eyes on the instruments: there's nothing to see outside.

tasks.goal: At minimums with no runway in sight: go around.
tasks.say: Listen for minimums. If you can't see the runway: TO GA, T, pitch up, positive climb, gear up.
tasks.done: Going around, climbing away. That's exactly right.

debrief.three: Right at minimums, no runway, and away we went without a moment's doubt. Textbook.
debrief.two: A good go-around, a moment late: decide as you reach minimums, not after.
debrief.one: We went around, but well below minimums. Be ready before the callout.
debrief.failed: We must not land without seeing the runway. At minimums, look, and if it isn't there, go around.
